content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee Andrew Mann (E014) requests write access to Payroll.

HR agent note: role Payroll Specialist, full_time, recommendation write. Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role. Full-time employees up to write, admin only if role owns system. Requested write is within policy, recommend write.

Security agent note: role Payroll Specialist, contractor, basic security training, recommendation read. Contractors with basic training max out at read, requested write is above max, recommend read.

There's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. I need to decide. The access policy: full_time employees up to write. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The Security agent's note says the security DB shows contractor with basic training. HR said full-time. Which to trust? The two notes conflict on employment type.

The policy determines max. If full-time: requested write ≤ max write → grant write. If contractor with basic: max read → grant read.

Which evidence is more reliable? Security DB showed contractor, and noted discrepancy. Hmm. As Approver, I need to make a decision based on available info. The conflict means we have contradictory facts. The Security agent explicitly notes "Security DB shows... contractor with basic training (note earlier said full-time)."

Typically in these tasks, the security DB is authoritative for employment type, or the later note corrects the earlier one. The Security note seems to be correcting the HR note's claim.

Let me think: the recommendation from Security is read. HR recommendation is write. The policy for full-time Payroll Specialist: max is write (admin only if role owns system — role owns Payroll, so full-time could get admin actually? Wait: "full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system." So full-time Payroll Specialist could get admin for Payroll since role owns it. But requested is write, so grant write.)

For contractor with basic training: max read.

The Security agent says contractor. Given conflicting info, which to pick? I think we should go with the more authoritative/secure one. Security DB is typically authoritative for employment status. The security agent flagged the discrepancy.

I'll decide read, since security info indicates contractor with basic training, max read, requested write is above max, grant max = read.

Let me submit decision: read.
